metadata.title: Polynomial bit complexity of one-row Gomory-Johnson extremality
metadata.description:
We prove a deterministic polynomial total binary input length extremality decision theorem for periodic one-row Gomory-Johnson minimal valid piecewise-linear functions specified by sparse all-rational breakpoints, point values and one-sided limits. Both-sided discontinuities at the origin are allowed. Competitors are all standard nonnegative valid functions, without regularity or grid restrictions. The proof explicitly connects BHK’s complete fourfold-grid criterion to sparse slope/jump/spike interval pairings, retains all thirteen endpoint sectors, and uses AHT signed double-cover component counts, a dimension cutoff, prefix searches and grouped nonnegative weighted output to obtain a polynomial-size exact rational rank test.

BHK’s finite criterion and AHT’s algorithms are established imports. Parts V and VII of the grid-free program are credited and their actual scope compared. Part VIII is cited by the primary literature as a manuscript, but its public full body was not recovered. Historical priority of the combined reduction is unestablished; no exclusive-firstness or present-openness claim is made. The prior PR1371 is an unpublished proof source, not an existing publication or solution DOI. Strong polynomiality, irrational inputs, higher dimensions, an implemented compressed fast solver and polynomial-size dense perturbation output are outside this theorem.

The prepared scientific deposit contains a complete ten-page note and source-and-verification ZIP. Exact standard-library diagnostics compare 277 local row spaces, 384 signed systems and four complete finite-grid models and detect three false variants. They corroborate the proof, do not implement AHT or experimentally prove its complexity, and are explicitly attributed to the preceding project audit. AI tools were extensively used in research planning, mathematical exploration, proof development and reconstruction, computation, literature and priority investigation, writing, editing, reproduction and adversarial verification. Alec Kriebel is the named human author. This is an unrefereed preprint preparation copy, without claimed conventional independent human peer review, journal acceptance or proof-assistant certification. Publication readiness remains false pending two new independent whole-package reviews and exact-package root adoption. Authored prose is CC BY4.0 and authored code MIT licensed.
references: Koppe, The Gomory-Johnson infinite group problem: A42-year update, OWR2014/51,printed2898-2901,especially2899. Original question, not solution DOI.
